Touchstones
Frenzy
Frenzy mode
A failed Resist roll (Resolve + Blood Potency) means the Beast takes over: Frenzy (Wrath) attacks the source of anger, Rötschreck (Fear) flees from fire or sunlight, Hunger feeds on the nearest vessel. Riding the Wave: the vampire may give in voluntarily and keeps a single purpose. The frenzy ends when the trigger is gone or the scene ends; press End Frenzy then.
Common triggers: provocation or humiliation (Wrath), fire or sunlight (Rötschreck), blood when Vitae is low (Hunger).
Banes
Auspice & Moon Gift
Choose an Auspice on Main.
Gibbous Moon
Auspice Ability: Prophetic Dreams
The Storyteller may grant prophetic dreams; roll Intelligence + Occult to interpret. After a night of 4+ hours' sleep, once you may declare an action or event was foretold: you or a packmate gain +3 to one action, or a Storyteller character takes -3.
Auspice Skills: Crafts, Expression, Persuasion · Renown: Glory · Gift affinities: Inspiration, Knowledge, Gibbous Moon
Half Moon
Auspice Ability: Darkness Into Light
Once per chapter, cure a werewolf of Death Rage (the target is Stunned for the next turn if in Basu-Im), or force one into Death Rage with Presence + Empathy + Primal Urge vs Resolve + Composure (works only on Uratha).
Auspice Skills: Empathy, Investigation, Politics · Renown: Honor · Gift affinities: Insight, Warding, Half Moon
New Moon
Auspice Ability: Closer Than You Thought
Once per chapter, choose one: move your Initiative to within 1 of a target's; close to use teeth/claws on one opponent not attacking you; or reduce Doors needed in Social maneuvering by 2.
Auspice Skills: Larceny, Stealth, Subterfuge · Renown: Cunning · Gift affinities: Evasion, Stealth, New Moon
Crescent Moon
Auspice Ability: Spirit Howl
Once per chapter, spend 1 Essence (no roll): a howl silent in the Flesh echoes through the Shadow. Lower-Rank spirits flee or hide, more powerful ones show deference; hostile spirits' Defense is penalised by your Wisdom.
Auspice Skills: Animal Ken, Medicine, Occult · Renown: Wisdom · Gift affinities: Elemental, Shaping, Crescent Moon
Full Moon
Auspice Ability: Tenacious
Once per chapter, ignore the effects of any Conditions or Tilts hindering you in combat for two turns (they are not resolved).
Auspice Skills: Brawl, Intimidation, Survival · Renown: Purity · Gift affinities: Dominance, Strength, Full Moon

Touchstones
Death Rage mode (Basu-Im)
Entered automatically when Wasu-Im! fails. The sheet shifts to Gauru (or Ur'Khar if the Form of the Firstborn toggle is on), turns red, and dims what Kuruth does not allow: in the Death Rage the werewolf attacks the nearest target each turn, cannot take social, mental or complex actions, and acts on instinct. Kept usable: Brawl, Athletics, Intimidation, Stealth, Survival, attacks and the dice roller. Death Rage ends only when the werewolf is killed or its duration (set by Primal Urge) runs out; in play the scene often cuts away first. Afterwards the werewolf remembers nothing of the time in Basu-Im. Press End Death Rage then.
Armor
GeneralBallisticStr req.Def pen.Spd pen.
Only worn armor counts. Several worn pieces: highest General and Ballistic, Str req. and penalties add up. Ballistic applies first against firearms.

Gauru
StrDexStaManSizeDefInitSpeedHealthPerc
Teeth/Claws +2L (Init +3)Defense vs. FirearmsFull LunacyRegenerationRagePrimal Fear
Teeth/Claws +2L (Init +3): Bite and claws are natural weapons that inflict lethal damage and add +2 dice to Brawl attacks made with them. The listed +3 is an Initiative modifier while the werewolf fights with these natural weapons.Defense vs. Firearms: The werewolf may apply her Defense against firearms and other ranged gun attacks, which normally ignore Defense.Full Lunacy: Ordinary humans who see the werewolf in this form fall under the Lunacy: they panic, flee or freeze according to their Willpower, and afterwards remember a rationalised version of events (wild dog, big guy, nothing at all). The war form applies the Lunacy at full strength, with no bonus to the witnesses.Regeneration: The war form heals at a supernatural rate: each turn the werewolf may reflexively heal one point of bashing or lethal damage. Aggravated damage is not healed this way.Rage: The war form is pure aggression. Holding it is limited to Stamina + Primal Urge turns, and while in it the werewolf is driven toward violence: mental and social actions other than intimidation are restricted, and staying past the limit risks Death Rage.Primal Fear: The war form terrifies even the supernatural. Beyond the human Lunacy, other creatures who see it may need to steel themselves before acting against it (Storyteller adjudicates).Select a feature above to read what it does.
Stable Gauru (Ur'Khar enabled): Strength +2 instead of the usual bonus, held at will with no time limit, normal regeneration. The stat grid already uses these values.

Harmony
HShapeshiftingFlesh / Spirit
10Instant action, always costs 1 EssenceLeans hard toward Spirit: the werewolf drifts from the physical world and human ties.
9Instant action, always costs 1 EssenceLeans hard toward Spirit: the werewolf drifts from the physical world and human ties.
8Instant action free, or reflexive for 1 EssenceBalanced, slightly spirit-leaning.
7Instant action free, or reflexive for 1 EssenceBalanced, slightly spirit-leaning.
6Reflexive, no costBalanced: neither side dominates.
5Reflexive, no costBalanced: neither side dominates.
4Reflexive, no costBalanced: neither side dominates.
3Reflexive, no cost; involuntary shifts each scene, resisting is an instant action or 1 EssenceLeans toward Flesh: driven by hunger and instinct, spirits react badly.
2Reflexive, no cost; involuntary shifts each scene, resisting is an instant action or 1 EssenceLeans toward Flesh: driven by hunger and instinct, spirits react badly.
1Reflexive, no cost; involuntary shifts each scene, resisting needs an instant action and 1 EssenceLost to one side: severe Flesh or Spirit effects; the Storyteller may take the character.
0Reflexive, no cost; involuntary shifts each scene, resisting needs an instant action and 1 EssenceLost to one side: severe Flesh or Spirit effects; the Storyteller may take the character.
Breaking points: Harmony is lost by acts that betray either the Flesh (denying the wolf, living as a mere human) or the Spirit (cruelty to spirits, neglecting the duty of the hunt); which side was sinned against decides the direction of the drift.
